set_message.text: Skipping...Error messages are possible. They are an effect of the skip. Mission continues as normal. Confirm error(s)

crew reboard snapshot.#comment: Second dispatch accepted while the crew is outside (deboarding in progress or finished walking): the positions of the crew actors that exist now survive reload_mission in L:REBOARD_* (LAT/LON), and crew reboard interrupted crew recreates them there at the start of crew boarding so they walk back to their doors from where they are. An actor that does not exist is not stored: its seat was never left, or the normal boarding handles it.

crew reboard interrupted crew.#comment: Boarding of the crew that was outside when the second dispatch was accepted (see crew reboard snapshot). Same door, seat trigger and payload station as deboarding, in the reverse direction, starting from the stored position.

then.#comment: Sarah voice https://www.naturalreaders.com/online/ voice EN Bella

voice app connect.#comment: Voice app mode (L:AUDIOINHIBIT 1, voice code APP): connects to the voice server of the HPG Mission Companion at once, declares the voice pack EN (version 2 at least), makes the checklist voice (actor 11) the voice of every text without an actor tag and asks for new crew names. The pack texts are chosen by the program when the mission increments the LVARs L:xxxAPPnn; free texts (dispatch) are spoken with speak.

voice dispatcher publish.#comment: Tells the Mission Companion who the dispatcher is (user request of 2026-10-16): the tag <dsp:INDEX:CITY>, INDEX the position of the group selected on the CARLS in the static GRPID (global GRPIDX, -1 for the manual frequency), CITY the city of the base found by voice dispatcher name start (empty until found). The program keeps the last one until another arrives and says the full name of the group in its own words ({@DSP} in the pack, for example Leitstelle Zuerich); the mission keeps only the short names of GRPID. Called at the connection, when the group is chosen on the CARLS and when the city is known. Mission Companion only.

voice dispatcher name start.#comment: At the connection with the Mission Companion: publishes the dispatcher at once (city empty) and looks for the city of the base, the closest place (city, town or village) to mission_start_location within 20 km with the same kind of query as the closest hospital; the name of the result is base_city_Name. The wait for the base and for the query is at most 60 s and 45 s. The city is cleared at every call, so a city of an earlier mission never stays. When the query fails the program says the name without the city (Leitstelle, regional control center). Not run before a test in the simulator: the place query is not proven there yet (docs/testing/RUNTIME_VALIDATION.md).

voice new shift.#comment: New shift: the program draws new crew names when its option is Random names (the tag is ignored otherwise).

voice read dispatch.#comment: The dispatcher (actor 8, external radio) reads the dispatch description and objective shown on the tablet. The description is a text with a key, DSC.<incident ID_CARD>.<variant 1-4>, so a translated pack of the Mission Companion speaks its own text; the shown English follows the key and is spoken when the pack has no such text or it does not match. The vehicle of the missions 65-67 is read apart (DSC.VEH). Then the crew briefing. Only with the Mission Companion (voice code APP). Mission description runs for every dispatch received (first, next, custom menu); vrd_last stops a second reading of the same text.

voice dispatch triage.#comment: A dispatch arrived by RescueTrack (ready dispatch, first_dispatch: vda_pending yes) and the dispatcher read it: the crew decides before the pilot (the user) accepts on the tablet. The copilot asks the crew (DSA.ASK); with a second dispatch the fuel against the LOWFUELTHRSLD option (DSA.FUEL.OK / LOW), the two missions of the shift (DSA.MIS, the old PLT38 rule), the equipment (DSA.EQP) and the health (DSA.HLT) are checked; then DSA.GO and the question to the pilot (DSA.ASKP, or DSA.ASKP.B with fuel low or two missions done). The briefing with the dispatcher (voice briefing chat) waits for the acceptance: voice dispatch accepted, called by accept_dispatch. voice_dispatch_seq numbers the dispatches: a thread that is not the last one stops. Only with the Mission Companion (a wav pack keeps the counters PLT38 and PLT40).

voice dispatch triage run.#comment: Thread of voice dispatch triage (params seq = the number of this dispatch, second = 1 for a second dispatch). Lines 1.5 s apart; the chatter (declut 1) follows the AUDIO_DECLUT levels, the fuel warning, the two missions and the question to the pilot are always said. Then it waits for the acceptance (vda_open no, set by voice dispatch accepted) or a newer dispatch (voice_dispatch_seq changed) and, a minute after the question and without an answer, the dispatcher asks for it (DSA.NUDGE).

voice dispatch reassign.#comment: Called by ready dispatch when the new dispatch arrives: if the previous one was never accepted (vda_open yes) the dispatcher says it was reassigned to another unit (DSA.REASSIGN) and the waiting thread of the old one stops. The new dispatch is read afterwards by Mission description.

voice dispatch accepted.#comment: Called by accept_dispatch when the pilot accepts on the tablet: the answer to the dispatcher and the briefing (voice briefing chat) go on. A second dispatch reloads the mission, which ends every thread: L:VDA_RESP asks for the briefing to be said after the reload (loading macro, Cabin preparation completed). Without the triage (a wav pack, a custom mission) vda_open is not yes and nothing happens.

voice boarding chat.#comment: Crew conversation after the comm check (pack EN group board): pilot asks, copilot, doctor and the rear crew answer, pilot closes. New LVAR numbers PLT 47-48, CPL 65, PAX3 38, 90 (no wav yet). Only with the Mission Companion.

voice briefing chat.#comment: Crew briefing after the dispatcher read the dispatch (pack EN group brief). New LVAR numbers PLT 49-50, CPL 66, PAX3 39, 91. Starts with voice dispatch exchange (the pilot asks the dispatcher for an update, the dispatcher answers by mission class).

voice debrief chat.#comment: Crew debriefing on the ground at the base: LIFESCORE above 3 the good outcome (pack EN group debriefok, PLT 51-52, CPL 67, PAX3 40, 92), otherwise the bad one (debriefbad, PLT 53-54, CPL 68, PAX3 41). Only with the Mission Companion.

voice approach briefing.#comment: Two nautical miles from the accident, after the rescue vehicles information of the tablet (RESCUE_DISPATCHED): the dispatcher says in ONE sentence which vehicles are on scene and which are on the way (AVAIL 1 = on scene from the start, 2 = dispatched; the arrived flags move a vehicle to the scene), then the crew briefing: pilot (ground or hoist plan: hoist when there is no landing_spot or it is farther from the patient than ldg_spot_area_size), copilot (police or fire there or not), doctor (ambulance or not), crew chief (ground or hoist), pilot. Only information the crew has at that moment: the dispatch and the vehicles it announced. Pack EN keys DSP.VEH.* and APR.*; only with the Mission Companion (VCP APP). For a patient transfer and an organ transport (voice mission class TRF and ORG) the same moment, two nautical miles from the pickup point, has its own short briefing instead (pack EN APR.TRF.* and APR.ORG.*): no vehicles, no accident. Plan P (police): when the landing spot is chosen (customLZ), the police is on scene or on the way and the patient is farther than police_bring_crew_min_dist from the landing spot, the pilot says the distance and that the police drives the crew (APR.PLT.P with the distance in meters, rounded to 50, and APR.CHF.P), whatever the hoist or ground plan.

voice vehicle letters.#comment: The rescue vehicles of the tablet as letters for the voice texts: vb_s = the vehicles on scene, vb_w = the ones still on the way (A ambulance, F fire engine, P police; AVAIL 1 = on scene from the start, 2 = dispatched, the arrived flags move a vehicle to the scene), vb_amb N or A (ambulance), vb_sec N or S (police or fire). Used by the approach briefing and by voice crew vehicles.

voice crew vehicles.#comment: The crew confirms the rescue vehicles of the tablet in ONE sentence (pack EN CRW.VEH.BOTH, SCENE, WAY; nothing when there are none), instead of one short line for each vehicle. Mission Companion only (VCP APP): the old counters stay for the wav packs.

voice hospital proposal.#comment: After Query closest hospital, on the way to the patient: waits for the hospital (45 s at most, same fallback as the crew emergency route). Found: PRE_HOSPITAL is saved as before and, with the Mission Companion (VCP APP), the doctor says its name (pack EN HOSP.FOUND, the name is the hospital_name of the query); the wav packs keep the old line (PAX3 counter 6). Not found: with the Mission Companion the doctor says that no hospital was found and that the destination will be chosen by hand (HOSP.NONE).

voice say.#comment: One line of the pack (Mission Companion, voice code APP): <say:KEY> with the argument a for {0}. declut 1 = chatter, skipped by the AUDIO_DECLUT levels 1 to 3 like the other conversations. Used by the macros below.

voice mission class.#comment: The kind of the mission for the voice texts: ACC accident, SAR search and rescue (SARV overdue vehicle, SARC parked car, SARH person away from a house), TRF patient transfer, ORG organ transport, INJ injured only. From the locals SAR, scene_macro and accident_name of the dispatch.

voice objective.#comment: The dispatcher says the objective of the mission in a colloquial way, a text for each kind of mission (pack EN OBJ.*), after reading the description of the dispatch.

voice ground update.#comment: Updates during the ground operations (called every 2 s by on-site operations progress monitor). The team reports when it has news, not on a timer: a new stage of the operations (deployment, treatment with the condition of the patient from LIFESCORE, CPR, loading, return; a dead patient has its own report), a change of the time left (TIMERGND times the progress that is missing, in minutes, at most one report every 20 s), once who transports the patient. When nothing happens for 240 s and the pilot is alone (nobody else aboard, L:HMC_CREW_PRESENT) the pilot asks for the status; when nothing happens for 150 s and somebody is aboard, they make small talk (voice banter, only when voice calm allows it). Only with the Mission Companion (VCP APP). Pack EN GRD.*.

voice patient died.#comment: A patient died (called by multipatient registry event DIED): the doctor says it and the pilot answers; after the impact of a hard landing the copilot asks first and the lines are about the impact (the death cause is not the clinical deterioration). Not more than one reading every 20 s. Pack EN DTH.*.

voice hard landing.#comment: After a hard landing (threads landing hard, copilot line CPL 39): the pilot asks the crew to report, the copilot and the doctor (when aboard) answer. Pack EN HLD.*.

voice hospital approach.#comment: Some minutes before the hospital (random distance 3.5 to 6.5 km from hospital_user, phase 8 or later) the copilot calls the hospital with the minutes to go (distance over ground speed; 90 kt when slower than 40) and the hospital answers that it waits at the helipad: a patient aboard, an organ (whobringpatient organ) or a patient who died. Once for each dispatch (it waits for a phase below 8 before it can speak again). Pack EN HOS.CALL.* and HOS.REPLY*.

voice marshal notice.#comment: The presence of the hospital marshal (same condition as the optional marshaller at the destination hospital) is told by the dispatcher at a random distance of 0.9 to 3 km from the hospital, before the arrival. Once for each dispatch. Pack EN MAR.NTC.H.

voice hospital handover.#comment: At the handover of the patient at the hospital, started when the crew meets the ground crew (the stretcher team next to the helicopter, before the unloading is finished and before the tablet message Patient handed over to ED): the hospital team welcomes the crew, the doctor gives the handover and the hospital thanks. Pack EN HOS.WEL, HOS.HND, HOS.THX (HOS.ORG for an organ).

voice calm.#comment: 1 when the mood allows small talk: no crew emergency, nobody hurt (every crew member of the flight has CREW_LIFESCORE 85 or more and is alive), and with the param patient 1 a patient that is not dying, not dead and not in CPR (LIFESCORE 50 or more), with the param casualties 1 nobody died in this session (PATIENTS_KILLED_TOTAL). Used by voice cruise chat, voice banter and voice tip. Always 0 when the setting CREW CHATTER is REDUCED or MINIMAL, except with the param tip 1 (voice tip: the tips have their own setting CREW TIPS, independent from the chatter).

voice banter.#comment: Small talk of the crew (pack EN BAN.Y yesterday, BAN.M a match, BAN.C company): one of the three at random, four lines after a random 5 to 15 s. Only when voice calm says so (param patient and casualties as there); the messages are futile ones: options 1 and 2 are silent and the conversation stays coherent, so many times nothing is said.

voice tip.#comment: A tip of the crew about a function of the mission that pilots may not know (user request of 2026-10-14): a conversation of four lines, pack EN TIP.<topic>.1 to 4 (futile, spoken by the copilot, the doctor and sometimes the pilot), one after a random 5 to 15 s. Only when the setting CREW TIPS is on (the global CREW_TIPS, 0 or empty = on, 1 = off; kept in the profiles, independent from CREW CHATTER) and voice calm says so (param patient and casualties as in voice banter, param tip 1 so that the chatter setting does not stop it); with CREW CHATTER REDUCED or MINIMAL the Companion chooses the lower options of the message (all of them tell the whole information). The topics follow each other in a fixed order (SAV saves, MSL mission list presets, PRF settings profiles, CRW crew health, KIT kit weights, QLK quick links, DBG debug snapshots, MED medical options, FLR failures, CHT crew chatter, TOF how to switch the tips off) from a random start, so a tip is not repeated before all the others were told (the local vtp_next survives the reloads). The key is built from the topic code and the line number; a wav pack (no TTS) says nothing.

voice cruise chat.#comment: Small talk during the long legs of the flight, once each: to the scene (phases 4 to 6, more than 7 km from accident_location, above 300 ft), to the hospital (phase 8 or 9, more than 7 km from hospital_user) and back to the base (route 6, more than 7 km from RTB_location). Only when voice calm allows it (never with a dying patient, an injured crew member, or after a death); a short chat of the pack (CRZ.*, futile) and then, by a roll of 0 to 9, a conversation of voice banter (0 to 3), a tip of voice tip (4 to 6) or nothing; on the way back to the base a banter (roll 0 to 4) or a tip. When voice calm refuses the chat (CREW CHATTER REDUCED or MINIMAL, or the mood) the leg still offers a tip, 4 times in 10 (5 in 10 back to the base), because the tips have their own setting CREW TIPS and voice tip decides by itself. Chatter (AUDIO_DECLUT).

voice context publish.#comment: Context for the radio rule of the Mission Companion, published only in voice app mode (L:AUDIOINHIBIT not 0) and only when it changes: L:HMC_HELI_OFF 1 = battery master off and rotor stopped; L:HMC_CREW_PRESENT = bit 0 pilot, 1 copilot, 2 doctor, 3 HEMS1, 4 HEMS2 aboard (the seat tracker CREW_OUT_n flags); L:HMC_CTX_VALID 1 = both are published. The program decides how a line is heard (intercom, radio, external radio, voice, far voice, nothing: rules in the Companion, docs/architecture/VOICE_APP_MODE.md). L:HMC_CREW_EXIST = same bits as CREW_PRESENT for the crew members that exist (CREW_MEMBER_CAP), aboard or not; L:HMC_AT_BASE = 1 while the helicopter is in the wifi range of the start base (local wifiinrange = in), where the dispatcher reaches the crew radios even with the battery off; L:HMC_ZONE_TECH and L:HMC_ZONE_GROUND = zone of the nearest technician (engineera, engineer) and of the nearest ground unit or hospital staff (marshall, ambumedic, ambumedic3) from the helicopter: 1 up to 5 m, 2 up to 30 m, 3 up to 100 m, 4 beyond, 0 no such object (macros voice zone nearest, voice zone class). The battery master is not published: the Companion reads the aircraft variable L:H145_SDK_OH_BATTERY_MASTER. All of them are part of the change signature. L:HMC_CREW_MUTE (same bits) = crew members who must not speak: dead (CREW_DEAD_n 1) or hurt so badly (CREW_LIFESCORE_n below 15) that they are out of the conversation; the Companion keeps their lines silent. L:HMC_CHAT_MAX = the highest option number the Companion may choose for a message (the setting CREW CHATTER: FULL 6, REDUCED 3 = professional wording and the futile lines at their default, MINIMAL 1 = the default wording only, the futile lines silent); it is part of the change signature.

then.#comment: Pilot = the simmer: aboard from the end of the boarding (the right cockpit door closes after the pilot object is destroyed) to the deboarding (removed after the right cockpit door opens). PILOT_OUT is 1 in between; the visible pilot model (IMPL_PILOT0) is not used because an option can hide it.

technician pick.#comment: The technician of a scene (boarding at the start, arrival at the base): 0 male (Engineer 1), 1 female (Engineer 2). With the voice code APP it is random and published in L:HMC_TECH_SEX, so that the Companion speaks the lines of that technician (FRA.* and SARA.* have options for both) and the crew lines use its name. With the wav voice packs the lines are fixed (Frank at the start, Sarah at the arrival), so the pick is fixed too.

Ground time.#comment: HEMS registry visits sleep TIMEnSHORT once per clinical step, so TIMEnSHORT is level dependent. TIMEnMED/TIMEnLONG are still consumed by patient_wait_interval (ambulance and legacy hoist flows) and are not part of the HEMS visit estimate.

Rough estimate only: the clinical visit (TIMERGND, unchanged because it also paces the progress bar) plus a fixed allowance for the crew walking out, loading and walking back (90 s each way, 90 s per casualty), rounded to whole minutes.

voice dispatch exchange.#comment: Dynamic briefing after the dispatcher read the dispatch (called by voice briefing chat with the mission class): the pilot asks the dispatcher for an update by radio and the dispatcher answers with what is useful for this kind of mission (pack EN DSP.RQ and DSP.ANS.ACC, INJ, SAR, TRF, ORG), then, now and then and only with CREW CHATTER on FULL, the crew presents itself on board (BRF.INT.*, futile lines).
